overview: Docket (1930-32) on Japan's silk industry: price-slump intervention, barred Soviet silk-expert travel, bank-financed filatures, and a government silk sale to Gerli causing commercial complications.

people.name: William R. Castle Jr.
people.role: U.S. Ambassador to Japan; author of a referenced report on the silk-price slump

people.name: W. Cameron Forbes
people.role: U.S. Ambassador to Japan; sender of referenced despatch no. 136

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. diplomatic representative in Japan; sender of referenced telegrams and reports

people.name: Stanley K. Hornbeck
people.role: State Department Far Eastern Division official and author of a referenced memorandum

people.name: Paolino Gerli
people.role: President of the Silk Association of America and purchaser in a reported Japanese government raw-silk sale

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers on the Japanese silk industry
subfiles.about: An index to 1930–1932 State Department records concerning the economic condition, government regulation, financing, technical knowledge, and foreign trade of Japan’s silk industry.
subfiles.summary: Docket covers Japan's 1930 silk price-slump intervention, barred Soviet silk-expert travel, bank-financed filatures, and Neville's reports on a government silk sale to Gerli causing complications.

interest: Shows 1930-32 Japanese state intervention in silk, including a government silk sale to Gerli that caused complications.
